claim_summary: For every real \(\alpha>-1\), integers \(0\le p<q\) with \(d=q-p\ge2\), and complex \(c\ne0\), the weighted Bergman two-jet Gram kernel on the upper half-plane has exactly \(d\) distinct scalar zeros when \(d\) is even, \(d+1\) when \(d\) is odd and \(\operatorname{Im}c>0\), and \(d-1\) when \(d\) is odd and \(\operatorname{Im}c\le0\). All are simple. For odd \(d\) and real \(c\), the reduced zero polynomial has two further real boundary roots; every kernel in the stated class has off-diagonal zeros.
scientific_integrity: Primary source arXiv:2608.13193v1 first appeared 2026-08-13 UTC; all bibliographic dates are verified initial availability dates or nonassertive reference information. Sources do not provide independent validation; a mathematically equivalent unindexed result remains possible.
scientific_limitations: Counts scalar zero values for \(t=(z-\overline w)^{-1}\), not zeros of each fixed-\(w\) slice.
Restricted to \(\alpha>-1\), two nonzero differentiated evaluations, gap \(d=q-p\ge2\), and \(c\ne0\).
Excludes other domains, arbitrary finite or infinite differential sequences, and adjacent orders.
Finite checker tests are supplementary; the proof is analytic and relies on strict gamma log-convexity.
title: Parity law for zeros of separated weighted Bergman jet Gram kernels
